## Overview

Offline embedding refresh jobs are **scheduled batch processes** that regenerate vector embeddings for a corpus when conditions warrant a full or incremental re-embedding pass. Rather than recomputing embeddings on demand during retrieval, these jobs run on a fixed cadence, recompute embeddings for some or all documents in the corpus, and atomically swap the new vector index into the retrieval pipeline.

## When Refresh Occurs

Embedding refresh is triggered by:

- **Embedding model changes**: When the underlying model is upgraded, fine-tuned, or replaced entirely, existing vectors become stale relative to the new model space. A refresh ensures all vectors are in the same embedding space.
- **Bulk document updates**: When a large batch of source documents is added, modified, or deleted, a scheduled refresh can handle the corpus-wide update more efficiently than incremental per-document embedding.

## Operational Mechanics

### Cadence and Scope

- Jobs run on a **fixed schedule** (e.g. daily, weekly) rather than on-demand, allowing amortization of computational cost and reducing operational variance.
- Can operate on the **full document set** or an **incremental set** (e.g. newly added or modified documents since the last refresh).

### Atomic Index Swap

- New embeddings are computed and staged in isolation.
- The swap into the retrieval index is **atomic**, ensuring that queries never see a mix of old and new vectors mid-transition — all queries resolve against either the old or new index, never both.
- This prevents semantic drift artifacts where some results rank by old-model similarity while others rank by new-model similarity.

## Key Operational Concerns

### Model Versioning

- **Tag or version the embedding model per batch run** so that it is always clear which model generated each vector. This is essential for debugging, monitoring, and eventual rollback.
- Store model metadata (name, version, timestamp, parameters) alongside the vector index.

### Vector Drift Monitoring

- **Monitor distance between old and new vectors** in the corpus to detect semantic drift or embedding space degradation.
- Compute aggregate statistics (e.g. mean cosine distance, percentile shifts) to quantify how much the embeddings have changed.
- Flag anomalies (unexpectedly large or small shifts) to alert operators to potential issues with the new model.

### Blue-Green Index Staging

- Maintain two index instances: **blue** (currently serving queries) and **green** (staging area for new embeddings).
- After a refresh completes and passes quality checks, **swap traffic from blue to green**.
- If a **quality regression is detected**, roll back by reverting traffic to blue without data loss or downtime.
- This staging approach decouples embedding computation from query serving and provides a safe point to validate or abort a refresh.

- [[incremental-embedding-updates]] — for real-time or near-real-time embedding updates
- [[vector-index-management]] — broader operations around maintaining retrieval indices
- [[blue-green-deployment]] — the deployment strategy underlying safe index swaps

## Source Summary

This source describes offline embedding refresh as a scheduled batch process for regenerating vector embeddings when:
- The underlying embedding model changes or is upgraded
- Source documents are updated in bulk

The source emphasizes three key operational practices:

1. **Model versioning per batch** — tag or version the embedding model so each vector batch is traceable to its source model
2. **Drift monitoring** — track changes between old and new vectors to detect regressions or anomalies
3. **Blue-green index staging** — run the refresh against a staged (green) index, swap traffic atomically after quality validation, and maintain rollback capability to the previous (blue) index

## Key Claims

- Refresh jobs run on a **fixed cadence** rather than on demand, allowing computational cost amortization
- The swap is **atomic** to avoid serving mixed-model results during transition
- Incremental or full corpus re-embedding is supported
- Quality regressions can be rolled back by reverting the index swap
